title: Beyşehir Lake & Eşrefoğlu Wooden Mosque: UNESCO Seljuk Route
seoTitle: Beyşehir Lake & Eşrefoğlu Mosque: UNESCO Seljuk Detour
metaDescription: Plan a 2026 stop at Eşrefoğlu Wooden Mosque and Lake Beyşehir: UNESCO cedar architecture, Konya-to-Antalya driving route, and sunset spots.
quickAnswer: Built in 1299 just 100 metres north of Türkiye's largest freshwater lake, Eşrefoğlu Mosque in Beyşehir is the largest of the five UNESCO-listed Wooden Hypostyle Mosques of Medieval Anatolia. Located 90 km west of Konya and 210 km north of Antalya, it makes a rewarding 2- to 3-hour architectural and lakeside detour on a Central-to-Mediterranean driving route.

body.text: Travelers searching for esrefoglu mosque beysehir are usually driving between Cappadocia, Konya, and the Mediterranean coast—and looking for a genuinely substantive stop rather than a highway rest station. Beyşehir delivers both world-class Seljuk-Beylik timber craftsmanship and calm alpine-lake scenery without tour-bus crowds.
Why is Eşrefoğlu Mosque part of Türkiye's UNESCO Wooden Hypostyle Mosques?

UNESCO inscribed the [Wooden Hypostyle Mosques of Medieval Anatolia](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1694/) in September 2023 as a five-mosque serial property representing an unusual Islamic building type: stone-masonry outer walls enclosing rows of load-bearing wooden columns supporting a flat timber ceiling. Completed in 1299 by Emir Süleyman Bey, Eşrefoğlu Mosque is the largest and most structurally complete example.

According to Türkiye's [Ministry of Culture and Tourism World Heritage overview](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/EN-120287/turkiye-on-the-world-heritage-list.html), the mosque measures 31.80 by 46.55 metres and anchors a broader medieval complex originally built with a tomb, caravanserai, and bathhouse. Inside, 48 tall cedar columns with carved muqarnas capitals create a quiet wooden hall anchored by a turquoise-and-cobalt mosaic-tiled mihrab and a finely joined walnut minbar assembled without nails.

At the center of the prayer hall sits a sunken stone pit (karlık) beneath a skylight—historically filled with winter snow from the nearby Taurus peaks. As the snow melted slowly into the stone basin, it humidified the dry Anatolian air, protecting the massive cedar pillars from cracking over seven centuries.
How do you drive from Konya to Beyşehir and Antalya?

From central Konya, drive 90 km west along the dual-carriageway D330 highway to reach Beyşehir in about 1 hour 15 minutes. Continuing south to Antalya (roughly 210 km, or 2 hours 45 minutes to 3 hours), follow the modern D687 route through Derebucak and the Demirkapı Tunnel across the Taurus Mountains straight down to the Mediterranean plain.

As noted in the [Go Türkiye UNESCO Mediterranean guide](https://goturkiye.com/unesco/mediterranean-turkiye), Beyşehir sits right on the natural corridor linking Seljuk Konya with coastal Antalya and Side. The Demirkapı Tunnel has significantly shortened the Taurus crossing compared to older winding mountain passes, making a single-day Konya–Beyşehir–Antalya transfer comfortable in a private car.

body.text: What sunset views stand out along Lake Beyşehir?

Lake Beyşehir's eastern shore—especially around the historic 1914 Taşköprü stone regulator bridge, the lakeside promenade (Vuslat Park), and Karaburun Beach 15 km south—frames wide west-facing sunsets directly behind the 2,998-metre Dedegöl (Anamas) Mountains. Because the water stays shallow and calm in late afternoon, golden-hour light reflects cleanly across the reed beds and distant islands.

Locals refer to the western mountain silhouette as the "Anamas sunset," and photography conditions are sharpest in late spring (May–June) and autumn (September–October) when dry plateau air removes summer haze. Along the waterfront near Taşköprü, casual family-run restaurants serve grilled freshwater pike-perch (sudak balığı) and carp caught in the lake.
How long does the detour take?

Budget 2 to 3 hours for a focused Beyşehir detour: 45 to 60 minutes inside Eşrefoğlu Mosque and its adjacent courtyard complex, plus 60 to 90 minutes for a lakeside lunch and walk along Taşköprü. Add another 60 to 75 minutes if you swing north to Eflatun Pınar, the carved 13th-century BCE Hittite spring sanctuary.

items: Check daily prayer times before entering Eşrefoğlu Mosque; it remains an active place of worship with free entry and modest dress expectations.

Bring thick socks in winter—the stone entry vestibule and timber hall stay brisk between November and March (see our [Türkiye winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide)).
Look up at the painted wooden beams and down into the central karlık snow pit—both details are easy to miss on a rushed walk-through.
Schedule lunch along the eastern shoreline near Taşköprü for local freshwater sudak fish before crossing the Taurus Mountains toward Antalya.
Confirm winter snow-tire readiness on the D687 highland section if driving between December and March.

faq.q: Is there an entrance fee for Eşrefoğlu Mosque?
faq.a: No. Eşrefoğlu Mosque is an active mosque managed by the Directorate General of Foundations; entry is free, though visitors should dress modestly and avoid sightseeing during congregational prayer times.

faq.q: What are the other four UNESCO Wooden Hypostyle Mosques in Türkiye?
faq.a: Alongside Beyşehir's Eşrefoğlu Mosque, the 2023 UNESCO inscription includes Afyonkarahisar Ulu Mosque, Ankara's Ahi Şerefeddin (Arslanhane) Mosque, Sivrihisar Ulu Mosque (Eskişehir), and Kasaba Village Mahmut Bey Mosque (Kastamonu).

faq.q: Can I combine Eşrefoğlu Mosque with Kubadabad Palace?
faq.a: Kubadabad Seljuk summer palace ruins sit on the southwestern lakeshore roughly 60 km from Beyşehir town, though excavation areas can be temporarily closed to visitors—verify access before adding the extra 2-hour round-trip drive.

faq.q: Is Beyşehir worth an overnight stay?
faq.a: Unless you want to photograph dawn mist on the lake or explore Eflatun Pınar and Lake Eğirdir slowly, most travelers visit Beyşehir as a midday stop between Konya and Antalya.

faq.q: How is the road from Beyşehir to Antalya in winter?
faq.a: The D687 highway and Demirkapı Tunnel are modern and maintained year-round, though brief snowfall can occur at higher elevations between December and March.

faq.q: Are there English guides or signage at Eşrefoğlu Mosque?
faq.a: Bilingual Turkish-English information boards stand outside the main portal and inside the courtyard; for deeper Seljuk architectural context, arrange a licensed guide departing from Konya or Antalya.
